title: Web Security: Strict CORS, CSRF & Content Security Policy
learningObjectives: Configure strict Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) allow-lists with origin validation
Prevent Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) using `SameSite=Strict` cookies and double-submit tokens
Deploy strict Content Security Policy (CSP) headers without breaking modern frontend apps
keyTradeoffs: Using `SameSite=Strict` cookies vs `SameSite=Lax` for external inbound link navigation
CSP `unsafe-inline` convenience vs nonce-based strict script execution
commonPitfalls: Reflecting the client request `Origin` header dynamically in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` with credentials
Relying solely on CORS to protect against CSRF attacks
transferPrompt: How does CSP mitigate the blast radius if an XSS vulnerability occurs in your frontend?
